description: Akenon Studio's shared Renovate preset (design 6.4). Every managed repo's renovate.json extends it with "github>Akenon-Studio/.github". A person approves every update; nothing merges on its own. `env` caps pnpm at one worker to keep lockfile updates within Mend-hosted Renovate's 3 GB (.github#123; platform outgrew it and runs its own, design 6.4); Mend allows the name (`global:safeEnv`). The dashboard issue is how the automation failures report sees Renovate's problems, since Mend has no API (.github#130, design 6.8); the issue checks skip it.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes open at once, whatever the schedule.

schedule: before 9am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Minor and patch updates grouped weekly, to keep CI minutes down: one PR per repo (platform: a few, below).
Every repo calls our shared workflows at @main on purpose, so a fix there reaches every repo at once (design 6.2): never pin or update them (.github#143).
three.js is part of the animation contract shared by platform and animations: both move together, by hand (platform#53).
dependency-cruiser 16 supports TypeScript <6, and outside its range it can stop parsing .ts files without failing; a repo stays on TypeScript 5 until it moves to dependency-cruiser 18 (platform#53).
platform is on dependency-cruiser 18, which supports TypeScript <7 (platform#196). Add a repo here when it moves to dependency-cruiser 18.

platform's single grouped update ran out of Mend-hosted Renovate's 3 GB in one lockfile pass (.github#123), so it is split: one branch per app, one for the packages, one for the root and workflows, and one for workspace-wide dependencies (below).

Tools, and every dependency more than one platform package declares (checked 2026-10-11), move together in one PR, so the workspace never runs two versions of one. Add a dependency here when a second package declares it.
Lock-file maintenance rebuilds platform's whole lockfile in one pass, more than Mend's 3 GB allows: off there until it fits (.github#124).

Pins (an action or dependency fixed to the commit or version a tag or range points to now) open at any time in their own group: grouped with real updates they waited on every fresh release (design 6.4, .github#168). They keep the release-age wait like any update; a pin PR's reviewer checks each pinned commit is the release its tag names. Last, so it overrides the groups above.
